analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md. It bumps the date and, at head line 371, documents a new `DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE` (default `~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json`, read in `Service/VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift`). Per the patch, owner-only records hold fully verified managed-load weight hashes, each bound to every file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime. Startup registration reuses a matching record instead of re-hashing. The supplied units are unchanged base text and the patch excerpt is truncated, so I saw no other docs changes; I cannot confirm the full head text.

The security-relevant behavior is that weight-hash verification at registration can now be skipped on a stat-metadata match. This touches T-012 (operator replaces weights), T-027 (weight substitution), A-004 and TB-003. The record file is operator-controlled, because owner-only protects against other users but not against ADV-001. The supplied evidence does not show an HMAC or Secure Enclave-rooted binding on the record. I also cannot see whether a record can be hand-forged with a trusted hash plus the tampered files' current stat values, or whether mtime or ctime can be manipulated. The code and `Service/VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift` were not provided, and the docs describe only the intended contract. The model hash was already self-reported and weights unprotected at rest, so this is not a demonstrated regression. It is an unverified contract that integration or code review should examine.

No other doc rows changed security semantics. Existing statements, such as 'Fresh pre/post-load verification ... retain their existing rules', should be checked against how the new cache interacts with them. T-012 and T-027 may need updating to describe the cache's trust assumptions once the code is reviewed.
